g.text: Separate software lifespan from failure consequence
Lifespan guides maintenance investment; consequences still determine the required checks.
Simple and removable.Explicit scope, owner and retirement condition.Avoid silently accumulating dependencies.
Maintainable and owned.Stable interfaces, documentation and regression checksappropriate to the continuing responsibility.
Constrained and checked.Access, numerical evidence and execution boundariesremain essential even in a temporary tool.
Operated and verified.Explicit controls, recovery and continuing validation;reassess as users and responsibilities grow.

Capital One’s conceptual discussion establishes neither deployed disposable software nor zero replacement cost.Cheap regeneration does not reduce an error’s consequence. Growing use should trigger an explicit maintenance decision.
Sources: Capital One, Sonar and Two Sigma accounts. Qualitative judgment aid; specific checks depend on the workflow.
